campus_seasons: CAMPUS SEASONS FOR uwaterloo:
University of Waterloo. Use this school's America/Toronto local dates. Fall 2026 anchors below describe general undergraduate dates unless noted; professional programs can differ. Display windows are editorial only. Never infer a seasonal event tag from its date alone.
Set campus_season_ids to all matching IDs below, or [] when none match. Use explicit event content and school context, never a date alone. Display windows control filter visibility only; they are not classification rules. Classify announced future events even when a display window is not currently open. Do not copy season classifications from another school. Networking opportunities (employers, career panels, hackathons, conferences) belong in employers_on_campus, not a campus-season ID.
- homecoming (HOCO): Official school homecoming, HOCO, alumni reunion or explicitly associated campus spirit celebrations. Include a varsity game only when the source explicitly associates it with homecoming. A regular game or unrelated party does not qualify. Waterloo Homecoming: 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-19. The filter begins 14 days earlier as an editorial discovery window. Tag only an explicit homecoming, school reunion celebration, or named official homecoming program; generic football games and unrelated alumni talks do not qualify.
- holidays (Holidays): Campus or student-community events explicitly themed around a named holiday, such as Halloween, Thanksgiving, Friendsgiving or winter holidays. A break in classes or a date near a holiday alone does not qualify. Follow the school-specific country and cultural context. This school is in Canada; local Thanksgiving is 2026-10-12. Windows are editorial discovery periods, not school closure dates. Tag explicit holiday celebrations, meals, parties or seasonal cultural gatherings only; do not tag generic autumn or December events. Halloween is October 31; its October 17-31 display window is editorial and does not assert a campus event or closure.
- orientation (O-Week): New-student orientation, frosh, O-Week or explicitly designated beginning-of-term orientation/welcome programming. An ordinary club meeting, recruitment drive or generic party does not qualify without orientation or welcome-week context. International Orientation September 3-4 and First Year Orientation September 6-12: 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-12. The filter begins 14 days earlier as an editorial discovery window. Tag only an explicit new-student welcome, orientation, frosh or campus transition activity; generic early-term events do not qualify.
- exam_destress (Exam de-stress): Wellness, therapy animals, snack breaks, crafts or relaxation explicitly intended to ease midterm/final exam stress. Ordinary free food or wellness events do not qualify without an exam connection. Editorial visibility during this school's verified-term preparation periods. Tag only explicit exam or midterm stress relief, not generic wellness.
- finals_prep (Finals prep): Review sessions, study groups, tutoring, practice exams or exam-skills workshops explicitly preparing for final exams. General academic talks, midterm preparation and ordinary classes do not qualify. Fall 2026 general finals or formal assessments run 2026-12-10 to 2026-12-23. The editorial filter begins 14 days earlier. Tag only explicit final-exam or end-of-term assessment preparation.

discovery_rules: EVENT DISCOVERY METADATA:
These independent facts may overlap and do not replace the event category.
For boolean flags, use true only when the source establishes the fact, false when it explicitly rules it out, and null when evidence is missing or uncertain. Never guess from the category, host, or the word 'free' alone.
- competition: An event where participants compete for rankings, judging, prizes or a winner, including hackathons, case competitions, contests and tournaments. Classify this individual event, not other events mentioned in a shared caption. Practice sessions, ordinary workshops, application announcements, raffles, ticket giveaways, watch parties and award ceremonies without competitive presentations do not qualify. Use null when competition is unconfirmed.
- employers_on_campus: Networking opportunities: true when meeting people who can help students' careers is part of this event. That covers employers, companies, firms or industry organizations recruiting, presenting, hosting, co-hosting or sponsoring it (a company named as host or co-host, such as "Ramp x Blueprint" or "Figma x Sanrio", qualifies even for a social); career fairs, employer information sessions and co-op or internship sessions; professionals or alumni sharing their careers or networking with students; career-path panels and advice sessions on breaking into an industry, including ones led by upper-year students; hackathons, designathons, datathons, case competitions and pitch competitions; and professional, industry or academic conferences, symposiums and summits. Online events and events off campus qualify. Ordinary club socials, meetings and workshops with no company, professional or career element, language and gift exchanges, study-abroad, exchange-program and grad school information, wellness, cultural, religious and community-service events, food distributions and performances do not qualify. Require event-specific evidence in the caption or poster; a post with no event details, such as a link-in-bio or weekly roundup post, establishes nothing. Classify this individual event, not other events in a shared caption. Use false when the event clearly has no networking element and null when that is uncertain.
- sports_game: An actual scheduled athletic game, match, meet, or tournament involving an official school varsity team. Intramural, club-team, and recreational competitions, practices, tryouts, fitness classes, sports-club meetings, video games, and watch parties do not qualify. School affiliation or posting from an athletics account alone does not establish varsity participation. Use null when official varsity participation is unconfirmed.
- campus_season_ids: School-configured campus season IDs established by the event's theme or purpose. Null means unreviewed or uncertain; an empty array means reviewed with no matching season. Display windows control filter visibility, not classification. Event dates alone do not prove thematic membership.
